column1: # Accepted differences between the DBC oracles (cantools <-> canmatrix) in scripts/selftest.py.
# A listed difference is reported as "known", never as "pass". Columns (tab-separated):

column5: Data longer than the message (12 bytes for an 8-byte message): cantools decodes it (allow_excess), canmatrix rejects it (DecodingFrameLength). Both reject data that is too short.
Multiplexer value 3 selects no multiplexed signal: cantools rejects the frame ("expected multiplexer id 0, 1 or 2"), canmatrix decodes the signals that are not multiplexed.
S0 = 3 selects no branch: cantools rejects the frame, canmatrix decodes the signals that are not multiplexed.
canmatrix 1.3.3 cannot encode extended multiplexing (Frame.encode raises EncodingComplexMultiplexed); cantools can.

A PDU mapped at frame byte 2 (PDU-TO-FRAME-MAPPING START-POSITION 16): cantools 45.1.0 and canmatrix 1.3.3 both place its signals as if the PDU started at bit 0. AUTOSAR places them after the offset, so neither oracle can check a consumer here; the self-test records the oracles behaviour (scenario arxml-pdu-offset).
